content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: JSON is a common representation for HTTP payloads and application boundaries. Reliable APIs define stable resource shapes, validate input, report errors consistently, version contracts carefully, and avoid confusing transport status with payload content.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: Representing database records. Mapping relational records into JSON. JSON columns and document storage.; Database-specific JSON querying. Schema flexibility and consistency. Indexing JSON data where supported.; Deciding what belongs in structured columns versus JSON fields.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: JSON and Databases
content_blocks.code:
Relational columns: id, status, created_at
JSON field: provider-specific metadata

Keep frequently filtered and constrained fields in explicit columns when that suits the database design; use JSON columns for intentionally flexible attributes, with suitable validation and indexing.
content_blocks.expected_output: The data model should distinguish stable relational attributes from truly variable metadata, and database-specific JSON query/index behavior must be verified.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
